finding_under_review: dos-2 - Unauthenticated /metrics renders O(N) attacker-inflated stats while holding the same mutex every gateway request takes -> lock starvation
category: unauthenticated-denial-of-service / lock contention + unauthenticated information disclosure
reason: DOWNGRADE high -> medium. All quotes are verbatim-accurate at the cited lines, and the structural coupling is real, but the load-bearing impact ("~100% duty cycle on the global mutex ... the whole data plane stalls to a crawl") is refuted by direct measurement of the same code: mt.mu duty from /metrics saturates at 5.4-6.4% and is Theta(1) in N. VERIFIED: metrics.go:88 is exactly `func (mt *Metrics) QPS() []QPSInfo {` with `mt.mu.Lock()`/`defer mt.mu.Unlock()` at 89-90, the full-map walk at 92-100 and `sort.Slice` at 101 all inside the hold; metrics.go:16-33 rotate, 114 ConnInc, 115-121 ConnDec, 122 Conns all use the same mt.mu (field at metrics.go:42); routes.go:20 is the `故不做 JWT 鉴权` comment and 21-24 register the handler on the bare engine, outside the /v1 group that gets `gw.Use(gws.AuthMiddleware())` (routes.go:28); admin/prom.go:14-16 confirms the scrape really calls s.mx.QPS() once per request (under promMu at prom.go:113); prom.go:135-139 emits HELP+TYPE+sample twice per key; gateway.go:195/300/301/318 confirmed and, because MaxConnections defaults to 1000 (settings.go:32), every gateway request takes mt.mu FOUR times by default (Conns, ConnInc, ConnDec, Observe), not three; no eviction/cap/TTL exists on mt.stats (metrics.go:56-71, no delete anywhere) and mx is built once (main.go:65); no auth/token/IP-allowlist/timeout/concurrency-limit on /metrics, and main.go:126 binds all interfaces (`Addr: fmt.Sprintf(":%d", cfg.ListenPort)`) so the `建议仅内网` comment is unenforced; dashboard.go:137 + RuntimeStatus.tsx:34 quotes are accurate but that path is authenticated, so it is not an attacker lever. MEASURED (go1.24.4, GOMAXPROCS=12, verbatim copy of ModelStat/rotate/QPS/ConnInc/Conns + the per-key prom.go emit loop, run in %TEMP% - no repo file touched): QPS() hold = 0.1 ms @1e3, 1.6 ms @1e4, 18.7 ms @1e5 (stale 18.67 vs fresh 18.92 ms, so rotate's cost model is irrelevant); render CPU = 4.1/31/347 ms and body = 33.1 MB @1e5 with ~30-byte keys. Driving a 64-goroutine synthetic data plane (3 acquires/request) for 4 s at N=1e5 with 0/1/8/24 concurrent unauthenticated scrapers: mean gateway acquire wait 0 / 280us / 650us / 1.28 ms, p99 0 / 17.5 / 24 / 31 ms, >1 ms 0% / 2.2% / 5.4% / 6.5%, mt.mu duty 0.4% / 5.4% / 5.7% / 6.4%, scrape throughput 2.8 / 2.2 / 2.0 per sec. The hold is ~1/18 of the scrape cycle because the O(N) render runs OUTSIDE mt.mu, and promMu (prom.go:113) forbids holds from overlapping - so more clients do NOT raise duty, and since hold and render are both Theta(N) the ~6% ceiling does not improve for the attacker as N grows (~5% extrapolated at N=1e6, where the per-event stall would be ~190 ms). Hence latency inflation with ~20-31 ms tails on ~2-6% of requests plus ~0.35 s CPU and 33 MB egress per scrape - degradation, not starvation, and the filed "CPU low, process looks healthy" is self-contradicted by the 347 ms formatting cost. STILL WORTH MEDIUM: (i) an unauthenticated route does hold a mutex the data plane takes 4x per request, and the per-event stall scales linearly with dos-1's N; (ii) promMu + WriteTimeout=0 (main.go:126) + writeMetric's ignored write errors (prom.go:48-58) mean ONE connection that never drains the 33 MB body parks every other scrape indefinitely (measured scrape_cycle_max 3.74 s/3.95 s with 8/24 clients; unbounded with a stalled reader) -> monitoring blindness during the incident, at zero attacker CPU; (iii) prom.go:136 `l := `model="` + promEsc(q.Model) + `"`` leaks the entire never-evicted set of raw client-supplied model strings (gateway.go:334), i.e. private aliases and implicit upstream model names (gateway.go:351 path), to any unauthenticated caller - a concrete confidentiality consequence beyond the stated 'no auth on /metrics' architecture fact. Recommendation is sound (snapshot-then-format, zero-window skip, cardinality cap on label values, token/split-port /metrics, ReadHeaderTimeout), but note snapshot-then-format alone leaves a Theta(N) map walk under the lock; the zero-skip + cap is the real fix. Finally, dos-2 is largely dos-1's primitive priced a second time (verify-dos-1.json step 3 already claims this /metrics step), which argues against two 'high's for one knob.
exploit_sketch:
Amplification prerequisite = dos-1's N (one valid gateway key, ~100k cheap 404s -> permanent mt.stats entries at metrics.go:63). The /metrics side needs no credential and no rate limit.
A) Lock contention (bounded, ~6% duty, NOT a stall): while :; do curl -s -o /dev/null http://target:8080/metrics; done  -> measured 18.7 ms hold per scrape, p99 gateway-acquire wait 17.5 ms with one scraper and 31 ms with 24, >1 ms on 2.2-6.5% of acquires, duty stuck at 5.4-6.4%.
B) Monitoring blindness (cheapest unauth hit, 0 CPU): open one socket, send `GET /metrics`, read nothing. The 33 MB render blocks under promMu (prom.go:113-114) forever - no WriteTimeout (main.go:126), and writeMetric ignores write errors (prom.go:48-58) - so every legitimate Prometheus scrape queues behind it and the write handler goroutine + fd stay pinned.
C) Unauthenticated disclosure (works at default N): curl -s http://target:8080/metrics | grep -o 'model="[^"]*"' | sort -u -> full historical model namespace, including implicit upstream names, echoed as label values and never evicted.

measurements.conclusion: hold:render ~ 1:18 and both are Theta(N); promMu serializes holds to 1 -> duty ceiling ~6% independent of N => filed ~100% duty / data-plane stall is quantitatively false

mitigations_checked: promMu (prom.go:113) DOES bound concurrent mt.mu holds to exactly 1 - the bound the filer dismissed as only hurting pileup; the O(N) render sits outside mt.mu so it dilutes duty; the SPA's 5s /status poll is authenticated (routes.go:142) so it is not attacker-reachable; MaxConnections (gateway.go:195) does not cover /metrics (ConnInc only in Handle at 300) - confirmed as filed; TRUSTED_PROXIES/XFF irrelevant (no IP control on the route); no inbound body to limit; no eviction, size cap, zero-window skip, label-cardinality cap, auth token, bind restriction or per-route timeout exists anywhere; write errors are ignored in prom.go:48-58 so early disconnect does not shorten the loop.
